sections.label: The prompt, typed into Codex in Hydrogen
sections.text: The prompt, typed into Codex in Hydrogen: build a Fusion library from my Demo Board cloud library on the Adom wiki, with the real 3D model bound to every part.

sections.label: Codex finds the parts and their STEP models
sections.text: Codex finds the six parts in that cloud library, each with a real STEP model, and hands them to the Fusion bridge.

This is the hard part. A STEP file in the cloud won't render; only a Fusion design does. The generator's FINISH button opens dialogs no script can close. And it always loads the first package in the library.
That third trap puts a chip on another part's footprint, on the left. The fix puts it on its own, on the right.
So the order matters: one library per part, load that footprint, import the STEP, save it as a Fusion design, then write every cloud link into the library in one pass.

sections.label: Part 1 of 6: LAN7800
sections.text: Part one, the LAN7800. The generator loads its own footprint, the chip goes on top exactly as the maker published it, and it's saved to the cloud as a Fusion design.

sections.label: Part 2 of 6: CH340G
sections.text: Part two, the CH340G USB serial chip, on its own split library, so it lands on its own footprint.

sections.label: Part 3 of 6: STM32L431
sections.text: Part three, the STM32 microcontroller, in its 64 pin package.

sections.label: Part 4 of 6: 16 MHz crystal
sections.text: Part four, a 16 megahertz crystal, on its four pad footprint.

sections.label: Part 5 of 6: LED
sections.text: Part five, a tiny LED, its body sitting right on its pads.

sections.label: Part 6 of 6: 10 uF capacitor
sections.text: And part six, a ten microfarad capacitor.

sections.label: One library, every 3D link written in one pass, saved
sections.text: Then every cloud link goes into one library in a single pass, and Codex checks every binding and saves the library to Fusion's Library Manager.

sections.label: Codex reports back
sections.text: Codex reports back: six parts, every one with its real 3D model, saved to the Library Manager, in about ten minutes.
